objective: Give LocateAnything-3B the visual-prompt capability that NVIDIA released a LoRA script for but did not release weights for, using the official script and auto-constructed COCO/LVIS reference-target pairs. Then measure it fairly against Rex-Omni.
why_this_is_worth_doing: NVIDIA's released LocateAnything-3B weights do NOT support visual-prompt inference; the official wording is that it 'will be released in a future version' with no date, while the visual-prompt LoRA fine-tuning script WAS released in June. Producing that capability ourselves and measuring it honestly is a real engineering contribution. It is not an architectural innovation — the architecture, the script, and the default config are all NVIDIA's. Describe it as 工程复现 + 公平对照, never as a novel method.

first_shot_is_a_go_no_go.size: 50k-100k auto-constructed pairs, 2k steps. Do not open with 5k/10k.
first_shot_is_a_go_no_go.purpose: Decide whether the direction works at all. A cheap negative here saves a day.
first_shot_is_a_go_no_go.go_criterion: Visual-prompt outputs become structurally valid and category-consistent at a rate clearly above the untrained checkpoint's. Pre-register what 'clearly above' means BEFORE the run.
first_shot_is_a_go_no_go.no_go: Report and stop. A negative at 2k steps is a finding, not a failure.

data_construction.shape: Pick a category; crop a bbox of it from image A as the reference; take all bboxes of that category in image B as ground truth; emit as a visual-prompt sample with visual_prompt: true in meta.json so the official loader takes the visual-prompt path.
data_construction.scope_is_category_level: This trains 'box one bottle, find all bottles' — category-level visual prompt. That IS the new-SKU industrial story and it is the tractable target.
data_construction.explicitly_out_of_scope: Instance-level matching ('find THIS specific red cup in another camera view') is re-identification, needs cross-view/occlusion/pose data, and is not what category-level visual-prompt fine-tuning produces. Never let a category-level result be described as instance matching.

the_benchmark_gap_that_must_not_be_paper.problem: Claiming the result 'approaches Rex-Omni' requires Rex-Omni scored on the SAME constructed visual-prompt benchmark. That benchmark does not exist yet and would be built from the same COCO/LVIS source we train on.
the_benchmark_gap_that_must_not_be_paper.requirement: Hold out a split that no training pair draws from, preregister it with a digest before training, and run Rex-Omni on it under identical conditions. Without that, the only honest statement is about our own before/after, with no Rex-Omni comparison at all.
the_benchmark_gap_that_must_not_be_paper.forbidden: Comparing our visual-prompt AP against any published Rex-Omni figure computed on a different benchmark.
